messages:
alex_g: Heads-up — Customer ACME reports their CSV usage export for 2026-12-01 -> 2026-12-03 is missing ~45% of rows compared to dashboard and invoice. They say lines for midday on 2026-12-02 are absent.

maria_s: ack. any quick sample of the CSV? single shard or combined?

alex_g: Attached snippet they pasted:
```
customer_id,date,model,tokens
acme,2026-12-01T09:00:00Z,gpt-redwood-7b,420
acme,2026-12-01T09:05:00Z,gpt-redwood-7b,380
# ... big gap ...
acme,2026-12-02T23:55:00Z,gpt-redwood-7b,120
```
They say the dashboard shows continuous rows every 5m but file jumps.

jordan_p: did they request shard=4 explicitly? we had a backfill/repartition job last week that touched raw_shard_4. devops-bot, any logs? :thinking_face: 

devops-bot: Noted. There was a short-lived export-worker 3 crash on 2026-12-02 14:12 UTC that retried but some pages timed out. Job id: export-v2-20261202-03. Errors: "ReadTimeout: failed to pull page 7 of 12 from shard 4". Retry policy marked pages as skipped after 2 failed attempts.

alex_g: That's probably it. Customer said missing midday rows around 14:00-16:00 UTC. Could be the timed-out pages. But they also report invoice token_total matches dashboard not CSV. So our invoice pipeline used rollup source not the export API.

maria_s: We should repro and then offer to regenerate CSV. Repro steps: can someone run an export with raw granularity against shard 4 for 2026-12-02 and see if pages 6-8 are empty? Suggest curl: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage/exports?start=2026-12-02T00:00:00Z&end=2026-12-03T00:00:00Z&granularity=raw&shard=4" \
  -o /tmp/acme-shard4.csv
```

jordan_p: I'll run that now.

jordan_p: ran the export, confirmed rows stop at ~2026-12-02T13:57:00Z then resume at 2026-12-02T17:02:00Z. So a ~3h gap. HTTP log shows a 504 at page token=abcdef after 2 retries.

alex_g: OK that's a clear repro. Next steps?

maria_s: Propose: 1) Offer customer a regenerated full export (we'll run with no sampling and with increased retries). 2) Backfill the missing pages into their original export bucket and update manifest. 3) Add alerting on export-worker page timeout rate. 4) Short-term: add a note to invoices/support that exports may omit rows if export-worker hit repeated timeouts — but invoices are authoritative.

billing-sre: For context, invoices are produced from the aggregation pipeline (rollups), which is separate and didn't miss data. Token totals on the invoice/dash use rollup. So billing correctness unaffected. We will still backfill CSV to avoid tooling gaps.

alex_g: I'll reply to customer with that plan. Draft: "Thanks — we found a transient export-worker timeout that skipped pages for shard 4 on 2026-12-02. Your invoice and dashboard token totals are correct; CSV export missed rows due to retries hitting the threshold. We're regenerating the export and will upload a corrected CSV + manifest within 4 hours. Apologies for the noise." Sound ok?

maria_s: yep. Add: if they rely on exports for billing, recommend switching to rollup API or confirm invoices as source-of-truth.

jordan_p: One more action: I'll rerun the export with flags: `?force_full=true&max_retries=6` and stream to s3://support-repro/acme/2026-12-02-shard4.csv. I'll post link when done.

devops-bot: export job started (export-v2-backfill-1819502). ETA ~18m.

alex_g: thx. I'll send the customer note now and mark as high-priority. :wave: 

billing-sre: Logged post-incident ticket to add `export_worker.page_timeout_rate` alert threshold.

maria_s: closing loop: once backfill is available, upload the corrected CSV to the customer's export URL and mark thread resolved.

alex_g: resolved plan noted. Will update after upload. :eyes:
